transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because... well, my brain feels like it just stalls out. Like, I'll sit there at work with a test report open, or even just a simple CAD note, and an hour will go by. I just can't decide what the next sentence should be, or even which checkbox to click. It's like the gears are totally jammed. Which is funny, because I actually had to replace the transmission on my Honda Civic last month. The gears were literally jammed. I spent all weekend under that car, getting grease everywhere. My roommate was so mad because I tracked oil onto the kitchen rug. It's a nice rug, too—she got it at this little vintage market downtown. We used to go there every Sunday before they moved it to the new lot... but anyway, yeah, I just can't seem to think straight at work lately.
How long have you been feeling like this, and have you noticed any other changes in your mood, like feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

It's been going on since I was moved into the prototype-testing role. That was about a year and a month ago. I remember because it was right around the time the company switched over to this new inventory software, and it was just a total nightmare. Nobody knew how to properly log the 3D printer filament in the new system, and my supervisor, Dave, kept accidentally ordering the wrong resin. We had boxes and boxes of this weird flexible TPU resin stacked up in the breakroom for like three months. It smelled terrible, kind of like burnt plastic mixed with old coffee. I actually had to stop using the breakroom microwave because of the smell, which really sucked because I used to bring these amazing frozen tamales for lunch from this little place near my apartment. They make them fresh and then freeze them in these big batches, you know? I usually get the green chile and cheese ones... but anyway, wait, what was the second part of your question? I totally lost my train of thought.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like visiting the vintage market or eating your favorite tamales?

Yeah, actually. I used to love painting these little miniatures... I have a 3D printer at home for them. But my printer has just been sitting there with the same half-finished figure on it for months. I just look at it and feel nothing. It's supposed to be this elven ranger character I was making for a campaign my brother runs, but he hasn't been able to run it lately because he got a new puppy. It's a golden retriever mix, super cute, but it chews on absolutely everything. He had to replace his laptop charger twice already because the dog just gnaws right through the cord. I told him he needs to get that bitter apple spray, but he keeps forgetting to order it. I order almost everything online now, actually, because going to the store just feels like too much work. Even things I used to like doing to get out of the house, like going to yoga or taking a walk in the woods behind my complex, they just feel like chores now. It's just another task on a list instead of something I actually want to do.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried a lot of the time, even when there isn't anything specific that should be causing that worry?

Anxious? Not really. I don't just sit around worrying about nothing. If I worry, it's usually about actual things, like if I miscalibrated the tensile testing machine at work. We have this old Instron machine that's practically older than I am, and the grips are always slipping. I told Dave we need to order new pneumatic grips, but he said there's no budget for it until Q3. Which makes absolutely no sense because they just bought a brand new espresso machine for the executive suite on the top floor. It's one of those really fancy Italian ones with the dual boilers. My friend Sarah works up there and she said the coffee from it tastes kind of sour anyway. She actually prefers cold brew. We tried making our own cold brew at my apartment once using this giant glass pitcher I found at Target, but the glass was super thin and it shattered in the fridge. There was coffee everywhere, all over the crisper drawers and everything. It took us like two hours to clean it all up, and my roommate was annoyed again... um, but yeah, no, I don't really feel anxious for no reason. Just the normal stuff, I guess.
Have you been feeling tired or lacking energy most days, even when you haven't been doing anything physically or mentally exhausting?

Yeah, I'm just so tired all the time. Like, bone tired. It doesn't even matter if I sleep, I just wake up feeling like I ran a marathon. And I definitely haven't been running, I haven't even been on a treadmill in months. We actually have a little gym in my apartment complex, it's down on the ground floor next to the leasing office. It's not great, just a couple of treadmills and some free weights, but the AC in there is always cranked up so high it feels like a refrigerator. The property manager, this guy named Kevin, he says they keep it cold to prevent mold, but I think he just likes it freezing because he wears these thick wool suits every day. Who wears a wool suit in this weather anyway? It's been so hot lately, like record-breaking heat. My car's AC actually died last week on my way home from work, right in the middle of traffic on the interstate. I had to roll all the windows down, and the noise from the semi-trucks was just deafening. There was this one truck hauling what looked like giant concrete pipes, and... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, energy. Yeah, I just don't have any. Even just taking a shower feels like it takes everything out of me.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, I guess so. It's just this heavy feeling, you know? Like this dark cloud that just sits right on my chest all day long. It's kind of like that feeling you get when it's about to storm and the air pressure drops really fast. We actually had a huge thunderstorm roll through last night. The thunder was so loud it shook the windows in my bedroom. My roommate's cat, Barnaby, he completely freaked out and hid under the sofa in the living room for like three hours. He's this massive orange tabby, like 18 pounds, so seeing him try to squeeze under this low-profile mid-century modern couch was honestly kind of ridiculous. We got that couch at a thrift store down on 4th Street. It was such a steal, only like fifty bucks, but we had to carry it up three flights of stairs ourselves because the delivery guy never showed up. His truck broke down or something. It seems like everyone's cars are breaking down lately, what with my AC and all. But um... yeah, the heavy feeling. It's just there pretty much all the time now. I just feel really down.
Have you found yourself feeling worthless or guilty, even about things that normally wouldn’t bother you?

Yeah, I do. It's... it's like I can't stop replaying these tiny mistakes I make at the lab. Like yesterday, I didn't log the calibration temperature right away, and I just kept telling myself that I'm not just bad at my job, but I'm just a bad person in general. Like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me because of it. It's stupid, I know. My manager, Dave, he didn't even notice, he was too busy yelling at the supply vendor on the phone. The vendor sent us the wrong grade of aluminum for the stress tests. They sent 6061 instead of 7075, which is a huge difference in yield strength. You can't just swap those out, especially for the aerospace contracts. We had this one aerospace contract last year where the client wanted us to test these composite panels, and they were so secretive about it, we had to sign all these extra NDAs. The guy who brought the panels in, he was wearing these really weird, like, mirrored sunglasses inside the building. I thought that was so strange. My dad used to wear mirrored sunglasses when we went fishing at the lake when I was little. We'd always rent this little aluminum boat, and... wait. What did you ask me? Oh, about feeling guilty. Yeah, I just feel like I'm completely worthless, honestly. Like I deserve to be punished for every little thing I mess up.
